title: Researching Research for Ayurveda
subtitle: A Journey
description: A working account of how Ayurveda research actually gets done — from framing a question to identifying a solution.
long_description:
Most writing about Ayurveda argues for it. This one asks a narrower question: when you sit down to study a classical proposition, what do you actually do first?

It moves through the stages a real project passes: deciding which parts of the corpus carry a reproducible signal, turning that into a claim that can fail, designing the experiment that could fail it, and reading the result honestly enough to act on. The failure modes get as much space as the method — studies that were never answerable, endpoints chosen after the fact, conclusions that outran their sample.

Written for people who will run these projects: postgraduate scholars, research faculty, and R&D teams who need the reasoning that happens before a protocol exists.
highlights: Method as the subject, not an appendix
Covers the failure modes, not only the successes
For scholars, faculty and industrial R&D teams

title: Integrative Perspectives
subtitle: Ayurveda, Phytopharmaceuticals and Natural Products
description: A 51-chapter reference volume on integration in Ayurveda, centred on drug standardization and regulation.
long_description:
Integration is the word the field uses most and defines least. This volume answers it by assembly rather than argument: 41 contributors, each an established expert or IASTAM awardee, writing from inside their own discipline.

The weight sits on standardization and the regulatory apparatus — the point where a claim either survives contact with analytical method and law, or quietly does not. Around it the chapters work through phytopharmaceuticals, natural products and pharmaceutics, including where classical preparation and modern analytics genuinely meet rather than merely coexist.

It is built to be consulted, not read end to end. Kept within reach by people working on standardization, regulatory submissions, or the industrial development of Ayurvedic and natural products.
highlights: Reference volume — built for consulting, not linear reading
Standardization and regulatory practice at the centre
